outcome: Type of anesthesia used for cesarean delivery
Cesarean delivery rate due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate (NRFHR)
Cesarean delivery rate due to history of previous single cesarean delivery
cohort: Women with singleton deliveries from June 2020 to January 2022, comparing those with and without peripartum COVID-19 (563 with COVID-19 out of 26,827 total)
finding: Peripartum COVID-19 was associated with preterm deliveries, increased risk of DIC, urgent cesarean deliveries, and lower neonatal one-minute APGAR scores, but a lower likelihood of premature rupture of membranes and prolonged maternal length of stay.
mod_finding: Women with peripartum COVID-19 had a higher rate of urgent cesarean deliveries (75.5% vs. 56.1%, p < 0.001).
